decisions.reason: As a close-to-core organic line, its market potential should have become clear quickly, and with no continued website presence through 2021 the option no longer justifies the added SKU, certification, and shelf-space complexity.

This product is near the firm’s existing capabilities, so uncertainty should have resolved within two years, and the lack of later visibility suggests insufficient traction to warrant keeping it open.

Because this was an incremental extension rather than a radically new category, the firm would expect fast learning, and absent follow-up evidence by 2021 it is better to reallocate capacity to stronger lines.
This aspic specialty looks like a niche experimental option for the deli counter, and once early demand did not translate into sustained presence, a disciplined portfolio approach would close it.

Even though it received dedicated presentation at launch, it was still a flavor variant close to the core range, so by 2022 the missing continued presence points to limited payoff relative to portfolio complexity.
For a pâté variant closely related to the established assortment, the firm should by now know its value, and without signs of sustained marketing support the prudent choice is to discontinue it.
